newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-FORECAST-Australian interest rates poll - Sept.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-FORECAST-Australian interest rates poll - Sept.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) Board will meet today, the first meeting since official interest rates were cut by 0.5 percent to 7.0 percent on July 31, a move that surprised many economists.
Ahead of the board meeting, Reuters surveyed 35 economists on their interest rates outlook, asking three questions.
1) Will there be a rate change following the September board meeting?
2) What direction will the next move in interest rates most likely be?
3) When will the next rate move take place?
*One economist forecasting a cut, no time for the move.
Economists' expectations have swung firmly behind a cut as the next most likely move in rates since the 0.5 percent reduction in July 31 that took many by surprise.

While a cut is not expected in September, a fourth quarter cut is the most favoured next move in rates, with those still seeing a hike as the next move generally not seeing it until the second half of 1997.

The key to a further rate cut is seen as the labour force data in coming months. If the job market remains weak, and the third quarter inflation and wages rates show continued moderation as expected, the case may be set for a rate cut, economists said.

If a rate cut hasn't eventuated by the end of 1996, the likelihood of one happening diminishes, as by mid to late 1997 most economists expect the economy to be moving along quite strongly with good employment growth, and consequently a rate hike is more likely.

The table below lists the most likely scenario for rates that economists see at the moment, with many saying the probabilities are just in favour a fourth quarter cut. If, for example, the U.S. or Japan was to increase rates then some economists said the likelihood of a rate cut would diminish because of the pressure it would place on the dollar.
